module purpose: neorv32_cpu_pmp stores PMP configuration and address registers from CSR writes, returns those registers on csr_o, and checks either the next instruction address or a load/store address against the programmed regions to register a protection fault on fault_o.

use-case flows.value: PMP region configuration bytes (R/W/X, address-matching mode, lock) written from ctrl_i.csr_wdata into pmpcfg on a selected CSR write
PMP region address values written from ctrl_i.csr_wdata into pmpaddr on a selected CSR write
Stored PMP configuration and address registers returned on csr_o according to ctrl_i.csr_addr
The pmpcfg lock bit blocks later pmpcfg and pmpaddr writes and changes M-mode permission handling
Selected access address and privilege are compared against the programmed regions to form match, allow, and fail decisions
fault_o reports the registered access-fault result when debug suppression is not active
Reset clears pmpcfg, pmpaddr, addr_mask, and fault_o to zero

conceptual assets.concept: Programmed PMP permission, mode, and lock settings for each implemented region
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure and lock flows store per-region policy bytes in pmpcfg only on selected CSR writes and only while the lock bit is clear: csr decode at lines 113-115, gated update at line 127, permission writes at lines 129-131, mode sanitization at lines 133-140, reserved-bit clearing at line 143, and lock-bit write at line 145. Those stored bits directly control later address-write blocking at lines 170-172, region-match mode selection at lines 303-310, and execute/read/write permission decisions at lines 323, 330, and 337, so corruption breaks the implemented protection policy. Availability is also established because the bytes are held until reset at lines 124-126 and are read back on csr_o through lines 203, 236, and 190.

conceptual assets.concept: Programmed PMP region address bounds for each implemented region
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores per-region address values in pmpaddr on selected CSR writes: csr decode at lines 157-158 and gated updates at lines 170-176. The stored address is blocked when the region is locked, and for non-last regions a TOR-locked successor can inhibit the write at lines 170-174. These stored bounds are then used in the NAPOT and TOR comparisons at lines 285, 295, and 296, so corruption changes which addresses match a region. Availability is also established because the values are retained until reset at lines 167-169 and are read back on csr_o via addr_rd at lines 208-220 and 192, with the low returned bits shaped by the static g_c/TOR_EN/NAP_EN conditions shown there.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP access-fault decision for the current checked access
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate and report flows compute whether the current access must fault. The checked context is selected at lines 244-245, where acc_addr chooses between ctrl_i.pc_nxt and addr_ls_i and acc_priv chooses between ctrl_i.cpu_priv and ctrl_i.lsu_priv. Address comparisons are formed at lines 285, 295, and 296; match is then computed from mode-dependent TOR/NAPOT logic at lines 301-314; allow is computed from access type, privilege, and pmpcfg permission bits at lines 318-342; fail collapses the first matching region and the non-M-mode default at lines 351-355; and fault_o registers the reported result at line 363 when ctrl_i.cpu_debug is not asserted. Integrity is established because these lines define the implemented protection decision and its report. Availability is also established because, with rstn_i = '0' inactive, fault_o is updated on each rising edge at lines 362-363. The flow graph leaves match unreached because the address tests are recorded as comparison/control edges; the RTL at lines 301-314 is the authority for that computation.
